name: Kingdom of Italy

areaKm2.note: LoN Year-Book 1938/39 Table 2: Italy 310 thousand km2. The world_1938 'Italy' feature (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/master/geojson/world_1938.geojson) computes to ~306,500 km2 (low); a second 'Italy' feature is the Dodecanese (~1,950 km2 on the polygon, ~2,700 km2 actual), included in high only.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1940 = 44,470k (1941 = 44,830k, high). LoN Year-Book 1938/39 Table 2: 43,509k present population March 1939; 43.8M quoted for 1940 in the cited Italian military history page (low). Metropolitan Italy incl. Sicily, Sardinia, Zara and Fiume; colonies, Albania and the Dodecanese population excluded.

urbanization.note: HYDE via OWID: Italy 1940 = 49.6% urban (high; HYDE counts large agro-towns as urban). Mid 0.45 discounts this. Low = COW upop/tpop 1940 = 8,304/44,470 = 0.187 (cities over 100,000).

activePersonnel.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-5 (Zamagni): Italian armed forces 2,340k average for 1940 (high, includes the post-June mobilisation); COW NMC v7 milper 1940 = 1,634k (low). June 1940 mid ~2.0M Italian nationals in army, navy, air force and MVSN, incl. Italian troops in Libya and East Africa; colonial native troops excluded.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: universal conscription since unification left many trained classes; strength rose from 2,340k (1940 average) to 3,227k (1941) per Harrison Table 1-5, but equipment, not men, was the limit. (context page: https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/economics/staff/mharrison/public/ww2overview1998.pdf)

supportPersonnel.note: active minus P roles: navy (~170k), air force (~100k), artillery, engineers, Guardia alla Frontiera fortress troops, services and depots.

mobilizationRatio.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-5: Italian armed forces 3,810k (1942) and 3,815k (1943) = 0.085 of ~45M. High allows for total mobilised over the war (~5M, educated).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Reconstruction: on 10 June 1940 59 infantry and 3 Blackshirt divisions (Mollo p. 83 via cited page), binary divisions of 2 regiments (~6,000-7,000 infantry each, many under strength), plus ~9 divisions' equivalent of frontier guards (counted as support). Libyan colonial divisions excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Carcano rifle, unreliable Breda 30 LMG, few AT guns and trucks; artillery largely WWI

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: short-service conscripts; most divisions below full complement of men and materials

count.note: 5 Alpine divisions (cited page) at ~9,000-10,000 alpini each, plus Bersaglieri regiments of the celere and armoured divisions.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: light mountain kit, mule-borne artillery

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: regionally recruited elite mountain troops

count.note: 3 celere (mobile) divisions (cited page), each with 2 horsed cavalry regiments (~800-900 sabres) plus divisional cavalry squadrons.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: horsed cavalry with L3 tankette support

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: traditional regular cavalry

count.note: 3 armoured divisions filled with L3 tankettes; ~100 M11/39 'medium' tanks available in June 1940 (Mollo p. 87 via cited page); plus Fiat 3000 relics. Total ~1,300-1,500 L3 tankettes is an educated reconstruction. 1940 AFV production only ~250 (cited Italian military history page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: L3/35 two-man tankettes with machine guns; M11/39 with hull 37 mm gun

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: little combined-arms training

count.note: Educated guess: 73 divisions with 24-36 field pieces each (divisional regiment establishment 36, Mollo p. 84 via cited page) plus corps, army and frontier (Vallo Alpino) artillery; much of it WWI-era and ex-Austrian. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Italian_Army_during_World_War_II)

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: WWI and ex-Austro-Hungarian guns, horse-drawn; good 75/18 and 149/40 only in small numbers

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: competent gunners

count.note: Batteries. Educated guess: 75 mm and 20 mm Breda AA in Milizia DICAT batteries around cities and ports. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Italian_Army_during_World_War_II)

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: 20 mm Breda good, heavy AA obsolete, no radar

count.note: 542 fully operational fighters in June 1940, ~70% of them biplanes such as the CR.42 (cited page). Neulen p. 30 (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regia_Aeronautica): only 166 modern monoplane fighters (G.50, MC.200).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: CR.42/CR.32 biplanes; G.50 and MC.200 underpowered and lightly armed

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: experienced pilots from Spain, good aerobatics, poor radio and gunnery

count.note: Richards, RAF 1939-45 vol. I Appendix V: Italian first-line strength June 1940 = 1,529 aircraft; minus 542 fighters = ~990 bombers and reconnaissance aircraft. Of 3,269-3,296 aircraft on paper ~55% were combat ineffective (cited Italian pages).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: SM.79 a good medium bomber and torpedo bomber; BR.20 and Cant Z.1007 average; no dive bombers until 1940 Ju 87

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Spanish Civil War experience, weak in navigation and anti-shipping bombing accuracy

count.note: 6 battleships (only 2 operational on 10 June 1940: Cesare and Cavour; Littorio and Vittorio Veneto working up; Doria and Duilio in reconstruction) and 19 cruisers (cited page; 7 heavy, 12 light by standard references). Low = without the 2 battleships in reconstruction.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: fast modern ships, Littorio class excellent; no radar, no carriers, poor night-fighting kit

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: little night training; fuel shortage limited sea time

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: fast but short-ranged, no sonar or radar initially

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: limited by fuel

count.note: 116 submarines in June 1940 (cited page), the second-largest submarine force after the USSR; 8 in the Red Sea flotilla.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: large, slow-diving boats with toxic air-conditioning leaks

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: peacetime training; heavy early losses

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Comando Supremo weak, services poorly coordinated, Mussolini interfering; good individual commanders but ad hoc planning (Greece 1940)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25-0.5. Evidence: national conscript army with regional splits; alpini and some units strong, mass surrenders in 1940-41 (Beda Fomm)

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.25-0.5. Evidence: the war was unpopular; troops poorly equipped and supplied, though some units fought well

weapons.note: Anchor: between 7 (1905) and 8 (1943). Evidence: WWI-era artillery, weak LMG; 47/32 AT gun; SM.79 torpedo bomber

armor.note: Anchor: close to 7. Evidence: L3 tankettes and riveted M11/39 (30 mm); no tanks comparable to Pz III

ships.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: fast modern battleships and cruisers, but no carriers, no radar, no sonar of note

fortification.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8 (Maginot). Evidence: Vallo Alpino along the Alps, Taranto and Sicily coastal defences

logistics.note: Anchor: between 7 (railways) and 8 (motor transport). Evidence: few trucks, horse- and mule-drawn artillery; electrified rail mainlines; long sea lines to Libya

communications.note: Anchor: 7 (telegraph, telephone). Evidence: few radios in tanks and aircraft

isr.note: Anchor: 7 (aerial recon). Evidence: no operational radar in 1940; aerial and naval reconnaissance only

air.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: 70% of operational fighters biplanes; SM.79 good; engines weak

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-8 (Italy, % of GDP at current prices): 8% (1939), 12% (1940), 23% (1941).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: industry ~30% of Italian output in the late 1930s; agriculture still ~40% of employment. 1940 steel output 2.1Mt vs Britain's 13Mt (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Italy_during_World_War_II). (context page: https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/economics/staff/mharrison/public/ww2overview1998.pdf)

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: the 'battle for grain' made Italy near self-sufficient in wheat, but fats and feed were imported; little surplus. (context page: https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/economics/staff/mharrison/public/ww2overview1998.pdf)

annualCohort.note: LoN Year-Book 1938/39 Table 3(a): Italy census 21 April 1936, males 20-24 = 1,979k / 5 = ~396k per year.

armor.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-6 (Zamagni): 3.0k tanks and SPG in the 38 months June 1940-Aug 1943 (~950/yr); 1940 output only ~250 AFVs (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Italy_during_World_War_II).

aircraft_fighter.note: Harrison Table 1-6: Italian combat aircraft 3.3k (1940), 3.5k (1941), 2.8k (1942), 2.0k (1943, 8 months); fighters ~65% (9,157 of 13,402 Italian aircraft per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_production_during_World_War_II).

aircraft_strike.note: Harrison Table 1-6 combat aircraft minus fighters.

artillery.note: Harrison Table 1-6: 10k guns in the 38 months of war (~3,200/yr).

ships_major.note: 3 battleships and 3 cruisers completed 1940-43 (cited page; column mapping flagged as uncertain there), ~1.5-2 per year.

ships_minor.note: Harrison Table 1-6 (Zamagni): 'major naval vessels' 12 (1940, 6 months), 41 (1941), 86 (1942), 148 (1943, 8 months), mostly small escorts and MAS; destroyers and torpedo boats ~20/yr (educated).

submarines.note: Educated split of Harrison's naval series: ~30 submarines completed 1940-43.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: national (ANAS ~20,000 km), provincial and municipal engineered roads; many southern and mountain roads unsurfaced. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Italy_during_World_War_II)

railKm.note: Educated guess: state railways (FS) ~16,500-17,000 km plus ~5,000-6,000 km of concession lines; major lines electrified at 3 kV DC in 1922-39. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Italy_during_World_War_II)

majorPorts.note: Genoa, La Spezia, Naples, Taranto, Brindisi, Bari, Venice, Trieste, Palermo, Messina, Cagliari, Livorno.

merchantTonnage.note: LoN Year-Book 1938/39 Table 113 (Lloyd's Register, June 1938): Italy 3,290k gross tons, x1.5 to deadweight (mid). ~27% of Italian merchant ships were caught in Allied ports and impounded on 10 June 1940 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_Italy_during_World_War_II), so low = 73% x 3.4M GRT x 1.3.

supplyRangeKm.note: van Creveld, Supplying War ch. 6 (North Africa): Axis forces could not be sustained much beyond ~300 miles from Tripoli/Benghazi; the Italian army was short of trucks, so mid 200 km.

draftAnimals.note: Italy's horse stock 942,000 in 1930 (Rich and Wilson p. 653, table 59, via the cited page); with mules and donkeys (~1.2M, educated) ~2.2M equids. The army was largely mule- and horse-drawn.

chokepoints: Alpine passes (Brenner, Mont Cenis, Little St Bernard)

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar mountainous terrain (Alps, Apennines), Vallo Alpino fortifications and fortified ports; population support lukewarm, no deep strategic depth.

notes: Snapshot date 10 June 1940 (declaration of war on France and Britain). METROPOLITAN Italy: population, GDP, area and cohort exclude Libya, Italian East Africa, the Dodecanese and Albania (in personal union since April 1939). Forces COUNT Italian national troops wherever stationed (Libya ~200,000 incl. Libyan divisions, East Africa ~256,000 incl. ~200,000 native ascari, both per the cited Italian military history page) but EXCLUDE colonial native units. Colonial bases are listed in basesAbroad. Weakest values: artillery and AA counts (educated), L3 tankette count, railKm and roadKm (no fetched source). Ship convention: battleships and cruisers = ships_major, destroyers and torpedo boats = ships_minor; only 2 of 6 battleships were battle-ready on 10 June. Merchant tonnage converted to deadweight at x1.5.
